code: #' Run Population Projection #' #' Performs forward projection of the population using assessment model outputs #' and management procedure specifications. #' #' @param sim_env Simulation environment #' @param obj Fitted assessment model object #' @param reference_points Calculated reference points #' @param asmt_data Assessment data list #' @param mp_config Management procedure configuration #' @param y Current year index #' #' @return Projection results including projected catch run_projection <- function(sim_env, obj, reference_points, asmt_data, mp_config, y) {    n_proj <- mp_config$proj_opt$n_proj_yrs    # Extract terminal year numbers-at-age   tmp_terminal_NAA <- array(     obj$rep$NAA[,, y, ,, ],     dim = c(asmt_data$n_pop, asmt_data$n_regions, asmt_data$n_seas, length(asmt_data$ages), asmt_data$n_sexes)   )   tmp_terminal_NAA0 <- array(     obj$rep$NAA0[,, y, ,, ],     dim = c(asmt_data$n_pop, asmt_data$n_regions, asmt_data$n_seas, length(asmt_data$ages), asmt_data$n_sexes)   )    # Replicate biological parameters for projection years   tmp_WAA <- array(     rep(asmt_data$WAA[,, y, ,, ], each = n_proj),     dim = c(asmt_data$n_pop, asmt_data$n_regions, n_proj, asmt_data$n_seas, length(asmt_data$ages), asmt_data$n_sexes)   )    tmp_WAA_fish <- array(     rep(asmt_data$WAA_fish[,, y, ,, , ], each = n_proj),     dim = c(asmt_data$n_pop, asmt_data$n_regions, n_proj, asmt_data$n_seas, length(asmt_data$ages),             asmt_data$n_sexes, asmt_data$n_fish_fleets)   )    tmp_MatAA <- array(     rep(asmt_data$MatAA[,, y, ,, ], each = n_proj),     dim = c(asmt_data$n_pop, asmt_data$n_regions, n_proj, asmt_data$n_seas, length(asmt_data$ages), asmt_data$n_sexes)   )    tmp_fish_sel <- array(     rep(obj$rep$fish_sel[,, y,, , , ], each = n_proj),     dim = c(asmt_data$n_pop, asmt_data$n_regions, n_proj, asmt_data$n_seas,             length(asmt_data$ages),  asmt_data$n_sexes, asmt_data$n_fish_fleets)   )    tmp_natmort <- array(     rep(obj$rep$natmort[,, y, , ], each = n_proj),     dim = c(asmt_data$n_pop, asmt_data$n_regions, n_proj, length(asmt_data$ages), asmt_data$n_sexes)   )    # Extract terminal fishing mortality   tmp_terminal_F <- array(     obj$rep$Fmort[, y,, ],     dim = c(asmt_data$n_regions, asmt_data$n_seas, asmt_data$n_fish_fleets)   )    # Extract recruitment history   tmp_recruitment <- array(     obj$rep$Rec[,, 1:y],     dim = c(asmt_data$n_pop, asmt_data$n_regions, length(1:y))   )    # Replicate sex ratio for projection years   tmp_sexratio <- array(     replicate(n = n_proj, obj$rep$sexratio[,, y, ]),     dim = c(asmt_data$n_pop, asmt_data$n_regions, n_proj, asmt_data$n_sexes)   )    # Replicate movement matrix for projection years   tmp_Movement <- array(     dim = c(asmt_data$n_pop, asmt_data$n_regions, asmt_data$n_regions, n_proj, asmt_data$n_seas,             length(asmt_data$ages), asmt_data$n_sexes)   )   for (proj_yr in 1:n_proj) {     tmp_Movement[, ,, proj_yr, ,, ] <- obj$rep$Movement[, ,, y, ,, ]   }    # Execute population projection   proj_results <- SPoRC::Do_Population_Projection(     n_proj_yrs = n_proj,     n_regions = sim_env$n_regions,     n_ages = sim_env$n_ages,     n_sexes = sim_env$n_sexes,     sexratio = tmp_sexratio,     n_fish_fleets = sim_env$n_fish_fleets,     do_recruits_move = sim_env$do_recruits_move,     recruitment = tmp_recruitment,     terminal_NAA = tmp_terminal_NAA,     terminal_NAA0 = tmp_terminal_NAA0,     terminal_F = tmp_terminal_F,     natmort = tmp_natmort,     WAA = tmp_WAA,     n_pop = sim_env$n_pop,     WAA_fish = tmp_WAA_fish,     MatAA = tmp_MatAA,     fish_sel = tmp_fish_sel,     Movement = tmp_Movement,     f_ref_pt = reference_points$f_ref_pt,     b_ref_pt = reference_points$virgin_b_ref_pt * mp_config$reference_points_opt$B_x,     HCR_function = mp_config$proj_opt$HCR_function,     recruitment_opt = mp_config$proj_opt$recruitment_opt,     fmort_opt = mp_config$proj_opt$fmort_opt,     t_spawn = sim_env$t_spawn,     bh_rec_opt = mp_config$proj_opt$bh_rec_opt   )      return(proj_results) }

title: Testing Management Procedures via Closed Loop Simulations (Dusky Rockfish)
text: Next, define functions determine catches constrained translate fishing mortality within closed-loop simulation. general, helper functions establish feedback catch advice operating model. first function applies management rules constraints (.e., caps) total allowable catch (TAC). constraints applied user-specified function catch_opt_func, modifies input catch advice based management procedures defined later. next function converts (possibly constrained) TAC corresponding fishing mortality rate (Fmort) used operating model. function uses bisection algorithm find value fishing mortality achieves specified TAC region fleet combination. updated Fmort values stored simulation environment use next time step closed-loop cycle.
code: #' Apply Catch Constraints #' #' Applies management procedure catch constraints (e.g., caps) to projected catch. #' #' @param tmp_TAC Array of projected TAC values #' @param catch_opt_func Function defining catch constraints #' #' @return Modified TAC array with constraints applied apply_catch_constraints <- function(tmp_TAC, catch_opt_func) {   for (j in 1:dim(tmp_TAC)[3]) {     tmp_TAC[1,, j,1, ] <- catch_opt_func(catch = tmp_TAC[1,, j,1, ])   }   return(tmp_TAC) } #' Convert TAC to Fishing Mortality #' #' Uses bisection method to find fishing mortality rate that achieves target TAC. #' #' @param sim_env Simulation environment #' @param tmp_TAC Target total allowable catch #' @param y Current year index #' @param sim Simulation replicate index #' @param assessment_years Vector of assessment year indices #' #' @return Updated simulation environment with new fishing mortality rates tac_to_fmort <- function(sim_env, tmp_TAC, y, sim, assessment_years) {    # Find most recent assessment year   last_assess_year <- max(assessment_years[assessment_years <= y])   tac_year_index <- y - last_assess_year + 1    # Create grid of region-fleet combinations   rf_grid <- expand.grid(     r = seq_len(sim_env$n_regions),     f = seq_len(sim_env$n_fish_fleets)   )    # Solve for F that achieves target catch for each region-fleet combination   tmp_f <- mapply(     function(r, f) {       SPoRC::catch_to_F_singlefleet(         f_guess = 0.05,         catch = tmp_TAC[1, r, tac_year_index, 1, f],         NAA = sim_env$NAA[1, r, y + 1, 1, , , sim],         WAA = sim_env$WAA[1, r, y + 1, 1, , , sim],         natmort = sim_env$natmort[1, r, y + 1, , , sim],         fish_sel = sim_env$fish_sel[1,r, y + 1, 1, , , f, sim]       )     },     r = rf_grid$r,     f = rf_grid$f   )    # Update fishing mortality in simulation environment   sim_env$Fmort[, y + 1, 1, , sim] <- array(tmp_f, dim = c(sim_env$n_regions, sim_env$n_seas, sim_env$n_fish_fleets))    return(sim_env) }

title: Testing Management Procedures via Closed Loop Simulations (Dusky Rockfish)
text: MPs define catch advice generated applied within closed-loop simulation. MP defined includes rules reference point calculation, control rule shape, catch implementation. helper functions specify shape control rules used across different MPs. threshold rule reduces fishing mortality spawning biomass declines biomass reference point, constant rule maintains fishing mortality fixed rate regardless biomass status. list defines specific MPs used example. configuration represents different management strategy, varying strongly responds changes biomass whether catch caps imposed. MP following components example: Reference point options (reference_points_opt) — specify biological reference points calculated (e.g., target spawning potential ratio, biomass thresholds). Projection options (proj_opt) — define harvest control rule (HCR) recruitment fishing mortality handled projections. Catch options (catch_opt) — optionally constrain catches according management limits (e.g., catch caps). Users flexibility modify extend structure fit specific modeling objectives.
code: #' Threshold Harvest Control Rule #' #' Implements a threshold HCR where F is reduced linearly as biomass declines #' below the target biomass reference point. #' #' @param x Current biomass #' @param frp Fishing mortality reference point (target F) #' @param brp Biomass reference point (target biomass) #' @param alpha Minimum biomass threshold (as fraction of brp) #' #' @return Fishing mortality rate HCR_threshold <- function(x, frp, brp, alpha = 0.05) {   stock_status <- x / brp    if (stock_status >= 1) {     f <- frp   } else if (stock_status > alpha) {     f <- frp * (stock_status - alpha) / (1 - alpha)   } else {     f <- 0   }    return(f) }  #' Constant Harvest Control Rule #' #' Implements a constant catch HCR where F remains at the reference level #' regardless of stock status. #' #' @param x Current biomass (unused) #' @param frp Fishing mortality reference point (target F) #' @param brp Biomass reference point (unused) #' @param alpha Minimum biomass threshold (unused) #' #' @return Fishing mortality rate (constant at frp) HCR_constant <- function(x, frp, brp = 0, alpha = 0.05) {   return(frp) } assess_freq <- 2           # Assessment frequency (every 2 years)  mp_list <- list(    # 1. No fishing   # Serves as a baseline scenario. No assessment, projection, or catch is applied.   f0 = list(     skip_assessment = TRUE,     reference_points_opt = NULL,     proj_opt = NULL,     catch_opt = NULL   ),    # 2. F40% with B40% threshold   # The assessment is performed and reference points are calculated based on an SPR of 40%.   # A threshold rule (B40%) is applied, where F declines linearly as biomass drops below 40% of B_SPR.   f40_thresh = list(     skip_assessment = FALSE,     reference_points_opt = list(       n_avg_yrs = 1,       SPR_x = 0.4,       calc_rec_st_yr = 3,       rec_age = 4,       type = 'single_region',       what = "SPR",       B_x = 0.4     ),     proj_opt = list(       n_proj_yrs = assess_freq + 1,       HCR_function = HCR_threshold,       recruitment_opt = 'mean_rec',       fmort_opt = 'HCR',       bh_rec_opt = NULL     ),     catch_opt = function(catch, prev_catch = NULL, catch_cap = NULL) catch   ),    # 3. F40% constant   # Similar to f40_thresh, but no biomass threshold is applied.   # Fishing mortality remains constant at F40%, regardless of biomass status.   f40_const = list(     skip_assessment = FALSE,     reference_points_opt = list(       n_avg_yrs = 1,       SPR_x = 0.4,       calc_rec_st_yr = 3,       rec_age = 4,       type = 'single_region',       what = "SPR",       B_x = NULL     ),     proj_opt = list(       n_proj_yrs = assess_freq + 1,       HCR_function = HCR_constant,       recruitment_opt = 'mean_rec',       fmort_opt = 'HCR',       bh_rec_opt = NULL     ),     catch_opt = function(catch, prev_catch = NULL, catch_cap = NULL) catch   ),    # 4. F40% hybrid: B60% threshold with 3k ton catch cap   # Combines a precautionary threshold (B60%) with a hard catch cap (3,000 tons).   # This MP reduces F more aggressively at lower biomass and constrains annual catches   # to prevent excessive harvest in high-recruitment years.   f40_hybrid = list(     skip_assessment = FALSE,     reference_points_opt = list(       n_avg_yrs = 1,       SPR_x = 0.4,       calc_rec_st_yr = 3,       rec_age = 4,       type = 'single_region',       what = "SPR",       B_x = 0.6     ),     proj_opt = list(       n_proj_yrs = assess_freq + 1,       HCR_function = HCR_threshold,       recruitment_opt = 'mean_rec',       fmort_opt = 'HCR',       bh_rec_opt = NULL     ),     catch_opt = function(catch, prev_catch = NULL, catch_cap = 3000) {       pmin(catch, catch_cap)     }   ) )

title: Testing Management Procedures via Closed Loop Simulations (Dusky Rockfish)
text: core closed-loop simulation involves iterating years replicates simulate population dynamics, assessments, management feedback. simulation year, population updated according biological processes, recruitment, fishing mortality. feedback period reached, management procedures applied based latest assessment results , cases, skipped MP specifies fishing (e.g., F = 0). Assessment model inputs prepared using setup_em helper, model fit available data (via fit_model). assessment complete, reference points calculated, forward projections run, catch advice determined. Catch constraints caps can applied converting advice true fishing mortality rates used operating models next year. single-replicate loop serves building block running multiple replicates parallel, allowing us evaluate robustness performance different MPs repeated simulations.
code: #' Run Single Simulation Replicate #' #' Executes one complete closed-loop simulation replicate including population #' dynamics, assessments, and management feedback. #' #' @param sim Simulation replicate index #' @param sim_list Simulation configuration list #' @param mp_config Management procedure configuration #' @param assessment_years Vector of years when assessments occur #' @param years_to_use Vector of years with available data #' @param assess_freq Assessment frequency (years) #' #' @return List containing simulation results (SSB, catch, F, NAA) run_single_replicate <- function(sim, sim_list, mp_config, assessment_years,                                  years_to_use, assess_freq) {      # Initialize simulation environment   sim_env <- Setup_sim_env(sim_list)    # Loop through all simulation years   for (y in 1:sim_env$n_yrs) {          # Execute annual population dynamics     run_annual_cycle(y, sim, sim_env)      # Management feedback loop (after burn-in period)     if (y >= sim_env$feedback_start_yr) {       # Check if MP skips assessments (e.g., F=0)       if (!is.null(mp_config$skip_assessment) && mp_config$skip_assessment) {         if (y < sim_env$n_yrs) sim_env$Fmort[, y + 1, , , sim] <- 0       } else {         # Normal assessment and management procedure         if (y %in% assessment_years) {           # Prepare estimation model inputs           dusky_input_list <- setup_em(sim_env, y, sim)           asmt_data <- dusky_input_list$data           parameters <- dusky_input_list$par           mapping <- dusky_input_list$map            # Set indicators for unused data years to 0           asmt_data <- SPoRC::set_data_indicator_unused(             data = asmt_data,             unused_years = setdiff(1:sim_env$n_yrs, years_to_use),             what = c("FishIdx", "FishAgeComps", "SrvIdx", "SrvAgeComps", "FishLenComps", "SrvLenComps")           )            # Fit assessment model with error handling           fit_result <- tryCatch({             SPoRC::fit_model(               asmt_data, parameters, mapping,               random = NULL, newton_loops = 1, silent = TRUE             )           }, error = function(e) {             message(sprintf("Model fit failed for replicate %d in year %d: %s",                             sim, y, e$message))             return(NULL)           })            # If model fitting failed, return NA results           if (is.null(fit_result)) {             return(list(               sim = sim,               rec = NA,               ssb = NA,               catch = NA,               fmort = NA,               naa = NA,               failed = TRUE,               failure_year = y             ))           }            obj <- fit_result            # Calculate biological reference points           reference_points <- SPoRC::get_closed_loop_reference_points(             use_true_values = FALSE,             sim_env = sim_env,             asmt_data = asmt_data,             asmt_rep = obj$rep,             y = y,             sim = sim,             reference_points_opt = mp_config$reference_points_opt,             n_proj_yrs = mp_config$proj_opt$n_proj_yrs           )            # Run forward projections           proj <- run_projection(sim_env, obj, reference_points, asmt_data, mp_config, y)            # Apply catch constraints (e.g., caps)           tmp_TAC <- apply_catch_constraints(             proj$proj_Catch[1,, -1, 1, , drop = FALSE],             mp_config$catch_opt           )         }          # Convert TAC to fishing mortality for next year         if (y < sim_env$n_yrs) {           sim_env <- tac_to_fmort(sim_env, tmp_TAC, y, sim, assessment_years)         }       }     }   }    # Return successful replicate results   list(     sim = sim,     rec = sim_env$Rec[,,,sim,drop = FALSE],     ssb = sim_env$SSB[,, , sim, drop = FALSE],     catch = sim_env$TrueCatch[,, , , sim, drop = FALSE],     fmort = sim_env$Fmort[,, , , sim, drop = FALSE],     naa = sim_env$NAA[,,, , , , sim, drop = FALSE],     failed = FALSE   ) }

title: Testing Management Procedures via Closed Loop Simulations (Dusky Rockfish)
text: efficiency, simulations can executed parallel across multiple management procedures replicates. run_parallel_simulations function sets parallel cluster, exports necessary functions objects, runs replicate simultaneously. Results replicate collected stored arrays spawning biomass, catch, fishing mortality, numbers--age. Users can modify custom manner extract additional results necessary unique applications.
code: #' Run Parallel Simulations #' #' Executes multiple management procedures in parallel across all replicates. #' #' @param mp_list List of management procedure configurations #' @param sim_list Simulation configuration list #' @param n_cores Number of CPU cores to use  #' #' @return List of simulation results for each management procedure run_parallel_simulations <- function(mp_list, sim_list, n_cores = max(1, detectCores() - 2)) {    # Initialize parallel cluster   cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)   registerDoParallel(cl)    # load in packages   clusterEvalQ(cl, {     library(SPoRC)     library(here)   })    # export functions in env   clusterExport(     cl,     c("sim_list", "assessment_years", "years_to_use", "assess_freq",       "setup_em", "run_projection", "apply_catch_constraints",       "tac_to_fmort", "run_single_replicate"),     envir = environment()   )    # init results storage   sim_res <- vector("list", length(mp_list))   names(sim_res) <- names(mp_list)    # loop through each management procedure   for (i in seq_along(mp_list)) {      message(sprintf(       "Running MP %d/%d: %s on %d cores with %d replicates",       i, length(mp_list), names(mp_list)[i], n_cores, sim_list$n_sims     ))      # export MP to par env     current_mp_config <- mp_list[[i]]     current_mp_name <- names(mp_list)[i]     clusterExport(cl, c("current_mp_config", "current_mp_name"), envir = environment())      # run replicates in parallel     replicate_results <- parLapply(cl, 1:sim_list$n_sims, function(sim) {        set.seed(123 + sim)         tryCatch({         run_single_replicate(           sim = sim,           sim_list = sim_list,           mp_config = current_mp_config,           assessment_years = assessment_years,           years_to_use = years_to_use,           assess_freq = assess_freq         )       }, error = function(e) {         list(error = TRUE, message = as.character(e), sim = sim)       })     })      # get dimensions from first replicate     n_regions <- dim(replicate_results[[1]]$ssb)[2]     n_years <- dim(replicate_results[[1]]$ssb)[3]     n_ages <- dim(replicate_results[[1]]$naa)[5]     n_sexes <- dim(replicate_results[[1]]$naa)[6]     n_fish_fleets <- dim(replicate_results[[1]]$fmort)[4]      # init result arrays     sim_res[[i]] <- list(       mp_name = names(mp_list)[i],       rec = array(dim = c(n_regions, n_years, sim_list$n_sims)),       ssb = array(dim = c(n_regions, n_years, sim_list$n_sims)),       catch = array(dim = c(n_regions, n_years, n_fish_fleets, sim_list$n_sims)),       fmort = array(dim = c(n_regions, n_years, n_fish_fleets, sim_list$n_sims)),       naa = array(dim = c(n_regions, n_years, n_ages, n_sexes, sim_list$n_sims))     )      # populate result arrays from replicate results     for (sim in 1:sim_list$n_sims) {       sim_res[[i]]$rec[, , sim] <- replicate_results[[sim]]$rec[1,,,]       sim_res[[i]]$ssb[, , sim] <- replicate_results[[sim]]$ssb[1,,,]       sim_res[[i]]$catch[, , , sim] <- replicate_results[[sim]]$catch[,,1,,]       sim_res[[i]]$fmort[, , , sim] <- replicate_results[[sim]]$fmort[,,1,,]       sim_res[[i]]$naa[, , , , sim] <- replicate_results[[sim]]$naa[1,,-n_years,1,,,1]     }    }    # reset parallel cluster   stopCluster(cl)    return(sim_res) }

Two demographic scenarios used condition future recruitment dynamics simulation, include rand crash scenarios. rand scenario, recruitment resampled input data reflect natural variability year--year recruitment. generates multiple stochastic replicates maintain historical patterns incorporating random variability. contrast, crash scenario simulates future recruitment mimic population crashes, followed recovery inputs R0_input h_input set produce period low recruitment (crash) subsequent rebound, providing scenario test management procedure performance extreme population dynamics. assessment conducted regular frequency (assess_freq; 2 years) burn-period, data available specified intervals (data_yr_freq; 2 years),
code: # Extract model components from dusky model data <- dusky_rtmb_model$data rep <- dusky_rtmb_model$rep parameters <- dusky_rtmb_model$parameters mapping <- dusky_rtmb_model$mapping sd_rep <- dusky_rtmb_model$sdrep  # Define operating model parameters closed_loop_yrs <- 50      # Years to project forward n_years <- length(data$years)  # number of years burnin_years <- 1:length(data$years)  # Historical conditioning period n_sims <- 100              # Number of replicate simulations assess_freq <- 2           # Assessment frequency (every 2 years) data_yr_freq <- 2          # Data collection frequency n_regions <- 1            # number of regions n_pop <- 1  # number of populations  # Condition closed-loop simulations set.seed(123)  # random recruitment sim_list_rand <- condition_closed_loop_simulations(   closed_loop_yrs = closed_loop_yrs,   n_sims = n_sims,   data = data,   parameters = parameters,   mapping = mapping,   sd_rep = sd_rep,   rep = rep,   random = NULL,   recruitment_opt = 'resample_from_input',   ISS_FishAgeComps_fill = "F_pattern",   ISS_FishLenComps_fill = "F_pattern" )  # beverton holt crash and recover # setup R0 input to mimic crash scenario R0_input <- array(0, dim = c(n_pop, n_regions, n_years + closed_loop_yrs)) R0_input[,,1:47] <- exp(parameters$ln_global_R0) # mean recruitment from EM R0_input[,,48:70] <- 2.5 # BH recruitment with crash R0 R0_input[,,71:98] <- 12 # BH recruitment with rebound R0 R0_input <- replicate(n = n_sims, R0_input)  # setup h input to mimic crash scenario h_input <- array(0, dim = c(n_pop, n_regions, n_years + closed_loop_yrs)) h_input[,,1:47] <- 0.999 # mean recruitment from EM h_input[,,48:70] <- 0.5 # steepness in crash h_input[,,71:98] <- 0.75 # steepness in rebound h_input <- replicate(n = n_sims, h_input)  sim_list_crash <- condition_closed_loop_simulations(   closed_loop_yrs = closed_loop_yrs,   n_sims = n_sims,   data = data,   parameters = parameters,   mapping = mapping,   sd_rep = sd_rep,   rep = rep,   random = NULL,   recruitment_opt = 'bh_rec',   ISS_FishAgeComps_fill = "F_pattern",   ISS_FishLenComps_fill = "F_pattern",   R0_input = R0_input,   h_input = h_input )  # Define assessment and data years assessment_years <- seq(sim_list_rand$feedback_start_yr, sim_list_rand$n_yrs, assess_freq) years_to_use <- c(burnin_years, seq(sim_list_rand$feedback_start_yr, sim_list_rand$n_yrs, data_yr_freq))

text: simulations performed, can extract results summarize visualization. , extract spawning stock biomass, recruitment, catch, fishing mortality rates. summarize quantities across time-series (within time point) median associated 95% simulation intervals.
code: for(i in 1:length(sim_all)) {    # extract out recruitment scenario   sim_tmp <- sim_all[[i]]    # get mp specific results   for(j in 1:length(sim_tmp)) {     # get ssb     tmp_ssb <- reshape2::melt(sim_tmp[[j]]$ssb) %>%       rename(Region = Var1, Year = Var2, Sim = Var3, SSB = value) %>%       mutate(MP = sim_tmp[[j]]$mp_name,              Scenario = names(sim_all)[i])      # get rec     tmp_rec <- reshape2::melt(sim_tmp[[j]]$rec) %>%       rename(Region = Var1, Year = Var2, Sim = Var3, Rec = value) %>%       mutate(MP = sim_tmp[[j]]$mp_name,              Scenario = names(sim_all)[i])      # get catch     tmp_catch <- reshape2::melt(sim_tmp[[j]]$catch) %>%       rename(Region = Var1, Year = Var2, Fleet = Var3, Sim = Var4, cat = value) %>%       mutate(MP = sim_tmp[[j]]$mp_name,              Scenario = names(sim_all)[i])     # get f     tmp_f <- reshape2::melt(sim_tmp[[j]]$fmort) %>%       rename(Region = Var1, Year = Var2, Fleet = Var3, Sim = Var4, f = value) %>%       mutate(MP = sim_tmp[[j]]$mp_name,              Scenario = names(sim_all)[i])      ssb_results <- rbind(ssb_results, tmp_ssb)     rec_results <- rbind(rec_results, tmp_rec)     catch_results <- rbind(catch_results, tmp_catch)     f_results <- rbind(f_results, tmp_f)   }  }  # get summary statistics for time series sumry <- ssb_results %>% # ssb   group_by(MP, Year, Scenario) %>%   summarize(median = median(SSB),             lwr = quantile(SSB, 0.025),             upr = quantile(SSB, 0.975)) %>%   mutate(Type = 'Spawning Stock Biomass') %>%   bind_rows(     catch_results %>% # catch       group_by(MP, Year, Scenario) %>%       summarize(median = median(cat),                 lwr = quantile(cat, 0.025),                 upr = quantile(cat, 0.975)) %>%       mutate(Type = 'Catch')   ) %>%   bind_rows(     f_results %>% # fishing mortality       group_by(MP, Year, Scenario) %>%       summarize(median = median(f),                 lwr = quantile(f, 0.025),                 upr = quantile(f, 0.975)) %>%       mutate(Type = 'Fishing Mortality')   ) %>%   bind_rows(     rec_results %>% # Rather, individuals natally home essentially represent skipped spawning (.e., contribute spawning biomass). Note populations 1 2 different dispersal retention probabilities (0.7 vs 0.3) despite sharing natal region, creating distinct mixing dynamics two co-occurring populations.
code: sim_list$Movement <- array(   0,   dim = c(sim_list$n_pop, sim_list$n_regions, sim_list$n_regions,           sim_list$n_yrs, sim_list$n_seas, sim_list$n_ages,           sim_list$n_sexes, sim_list$n_sims) )  # Fill in movement matrix stay_prob <- c(0.7, 0.3, 0.7)  # probability of staying in current region during dispersal season disperse_prob <- (1 - stay_prob) / (sim_list$n_regions - 1)  # spread remainder equally non_natal_rate <- 0.15 # non natal homing rate  for (p in seq_len(sim_list$n_pop)) {   nr <- sim_list$natal_region[p]   for (r_from in seq_len(sim_list$n_regions)) {      # Season 1: diffusive dispersal — mostly stay, some movement out     for (r_to in seq_len(sim_list$n_regions)) {       prob <- if (r_to == r_from) stay_prob[p] else disperse_prob[p]       sim_list$Movement[p, r_from, r_to, , 1, , , ] <- prob     }      # Season 2: natal return with straying     for (r_to in seq_len(sim_list$n_regions)) {       prob <- if (r_to == nr) 1 - non_natal_rate * (sim_list$n_regions - 1) else non_natal_rate       sim_list$Movement[p, r_from, r_to, , 2, , , ] <- prob     }   } }

title: Discard and Retention Modeling
text: estimation model mirrors OM structure estimates key parameters: fishery selectivity (logistic), retention selectivity (asymptotic logistic), survey selectivity (logistic), catchability, recruitment deviations, dead discard rate. function encapsulates full EM setup single simulation replicate.
code: setup_em <- function(sim_obj, sim) {    # get simulation data   sim_data <- simulation_data_to_SPoRC(     sim_env = sim_obj, y = sim_obj$n_years, sim = sim   )    # Model dimensions  input_list <- Setup_Mod_Dim(     years          = 1:sim_obj$n_years,     ages           = 1:sim_obj$n_ages,     lens           = sim_obj$n_lens,     n_regions      = sim_obj$n_regions,     n_sexes        = sim_obj$n_sexes,     n_fish_fleets  = sim_obj$n_fish_fleets,     n_srv_fleets   = sim_obj$n_srv_fleets,     n_pop          = sim_obj$n_pop,     natal_region   = sim_obj$natal_region,     verbose        = FALSE   )    # Recruitment   input_list <- Setup_Mod_Rec(     input_list        = input_list,     do_rec_bias_ramp  = 0,     sigmaR_switch     = 1,     ln_sigmaR         = array(log(0.5), c(2, input_list$data$n_pop,                                           input_list$data$n_regions)),     rec_model         = "mean_rec",     sigmaR_spec       = "fix",     init_age_strc     = 1,     equil_init_age_strc = 2,     ln_global_R0      = log(5)   )    # Biologicals   input_list <- Setup_Mod_Biologicals(     input_list    = input_list,     WAA           = sim_data$WAA,     MatAA         = sim_data$MatAA,     WAA_fish      = sim_data$WAA_fish,     WAA_srv       = sim_data$WAA_srv,     fit_lengths   = 0,     AgeingError   = sim_data$AgeingError,     M_spec        = "fix",     Fixed_natmort = array(0.3, dim = c(input_list$data$n_pop,                                        input_list$data$n_regions,                                        length(input_list$data$years),                                        length(input_list$data$ages),                                        input_list$data$n_sexes))   )    # Tagging and movement (none)   input_list <- Setup_Mod_Tagging(input_list = input_list, use_conv_fish_tagging = 0)   input_list <- Setup_Mod_Movement(     input_list         = input_list,     use_fixed_movement = 1,     Fixed_Movement     = NA,     do_recruits_move   = 0   )    # Catch, fishing mortality, and discards   input_list <- Setup_Mod_Catch_and_F(     input_list     = input_list,     ObsCatch       = sim_data$ObsCatch,     UseCatch       = sim_data$UseCatch,     Use_F_pen      = 1,     sigmaC_spec    = "fix",     ln_sigmaC      = sim_data$ln_sigmaC,     ln_sigmaF      = array(log(1), dim = c(input_list$data$n_regions,                                            input_list$data$n_seas,                                            input_list$data$n_fish_fleets)),          # Discard data (discard units are biomass fractions as default)     ObsDiscard     = sim_data$ObsDiscard, # observed discards     UseDiscard     = sim_data$UseDiscard, # using discards     sigma_dmr_spec = "fix", # fixing the deviations of discard mortality rate     dmr_mean_spec  = "est_all", # estimating discard mortality rate deviations     ln_sigmaD      = sim_data$ln_sigmaD # discard time series uncertainty   )    # Fishery indices and compositions (retained + discard)   input_list <- Setup_Mod_FishIdx_and_Comps(     input_list = input_list,      # Fishery index     ObsFishIdx    = sim_data$ObsFishIdx,     ObsFishIdx_SE = sim_data$ObsFishIdx_SE,     UseFishIdx    = sim_data$UseFishIdx,      # Retained age compositions     ObsFishAgeComps  = sim_data$ObsFishAgeComps,     ObsFishLenComps  = sim_data$ObsFishLenComps,     UseFishAgeComps  = sim_data$UseFishAgeComps,     UseFishLenComps  = sim_data$UseFishLenComps,     ISS_FishAgeComps = sim_data$ISS_FishAgeComps,     ISS_FishLenComps = sim_data$ISS_FishLenComps,      fish_idx_type        = "biom",     FishAgeComps_LikeType = "Multinomial",     FishLenComps_LikeType = "none",     FishAgeComps_Type     = "agg_Year_1-terminal_Fleet_1",     FishLenComps_Type     = "none_Year_1-terminal_Fleet_1",      # Discard age compositions     ObsFishAgeComps_discard      = sim_data$ObsFishAgeComps_discard,     UseFishAgeComps_discard      = sim_data$UseFishAgeComps_discard,     ISS_FishAgeComps_discard     = sim_data$ISS_FishAgeComps_discard,     FishAgeComps_discard_LikeType = rep("Multinomial", input_list$data$n_fish_fleets),     FishAgeComps_discard_Type     = "agg_Year_1-terminal_Fleet_1",   )    # Survey indices and compositions   input_list <- Setup_Mod_SrvIdx_and_Comps(     input_list = input_list,     ObsSrvIdx        = sim_data$ObsSrvIdx,     ObsSrvIdx_SE     = sim_data$ObsSrvIdx_SE,     UseSrvIdx        = sim_data$UseSrvIdx,     ObsSrvAgeComps   = sim_data$ObsSrvAgeComps,     ObsSrvLenComps   = sim_data$ObsSrvLenComps,     UseSrvAgeComps   = sim_data$UseSrvAgeComps,     UseSrvLenComps   = sim_data$UseSrvLenComps,     ISS_SrvAgeComps  = sim_data$ISS_SrvAgeComps,     ISS_SrvLenComps  = sim_data$ISS_SrvLenComps,     srv_idx_type          = "biom",     SrvAgeComps_LikeType  = "Multinomial",     SrvLenComps_LikeType  = "none",     SrvAgeComps_Type      = "agg_Year_1-terminal_Fleet_1",     SrvLenComps_Type      = "none_Year_1-terminal_Fleet_1"   )    # Fishery selectivity: logistic for total, asymptotic logistic for retention   input_list <- Setup_Mod_Fishsel_and_Q(     input_list              = input_list,     fish_sel_model          = "logist1_Fleet_1",     fish_fixed_sel_pars_spec = "est_all",     fish_q_spec             = "est_all",     ret_sel_model           = "asymplogist1_Fleet_1",     ret_fixed_sel_pars_spec = "est_all",     use_fixed_ret_sel       = 0   )    # Survey selectivity   input_list <- Setup_Mod_Srvsel_and_Q(     input_list              = input_list,     srv_sel_model           = "logist1_Fleet_1",     srv_fixed_sel_pars_spec = "est_all",     srv_q_spec              = "est_all"   )    # Data weighting (no data weights used)   input_list <- Setup_Mod_Weighting(     input_list     = input_list,     Wt_Catch       = 1,     Wt_FishIdx     = 1,     Wt_SrvIdx      = 1,     Wt_Rec         = 1,     Wt_F           = 1,     Wt_Discard     = 1,     Wt_D           = 1,     Wt_FishAgeComps = array(1, dim = c(input_list$data$n_regions,                                        length(input_list$data$years),                                        input_list$data$n_seas,                                        input_list$data$n_sexes,                                        input_list$data$n_fish_fleets)),     Wt_FishLenComps = array(1, dim = c(input_list$data$n_regions,                                        length(input_list$data$years),                                        input_list$data$n_seas,                                        input_list$data$n_sexes,                                        input_list$data$n_fish_fleets)),     Wt_SrvAgeComps = array(1, dim = c(input_list$data$n_regions,                                       length(input_list$data$years),                                       input_list$data$n_seas,                                       input_list$data$n_sexes,                                       input_list$data$n_srv_fleets)),     Wt_FishAgeComps_discard = array(1, dim = c(input_list$data$n_regions,                                                length(input_list$data$years),                                                input_list$data$n_seas,                                                input_list$data$n_sexes,                                                input_list$data$n_fish_fleets))   )    return(input_list) }

title: Discard and Retention Modeling
text: loop 50 simulation replicates, fit EM , store estimated SSB trajectories.
code: ssb_results <- array(NA, dim = c(sim_list$n_yrs, sim_list$n_sims))  for (i in 1:sim_obj$n_sims) {    # setup EM from above   input_list <- setup_em(sim_obj, sim = i)      # fit model   model <- fit_model(     input_list$data,     input_list$par,     input_list$map,     random       = NULL,     silent       = TRUE,     do_optim     = TRUE,     newton_loops = 3   )    ssb_results[, i] <- as.vector(model$rep$SSB) }

title: Discard and Retention Modeling
text: also compute relative error SSB across simulations years evaluate estimation performance. general, see model unbiased able recover true spawning stock biomass values, though estiamtes later demonstrate slightly larger biases (expected, given data availiability age-structured model).
code: library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) library(reshape2)  ssb_df_res <- reshape2::melt(ssb_results) %>%   rename(Year = Var1, Sim = Var2, Est = value) %>%   left_join(     melt(sim_obj$SSB) %>%       rename(Pop = Var1, Region = Var2, Year = Var3, Sim = Var4, True = value),     by = c("Year", "Sim")   ) %>%   mutate(RE = (Est - True) / True) %>%    group_by(Year) %>%    summarize(     lwr = quantile(RE, 0.025),     upr = quantile(RE, 0.975),     RE = median(RE))  ggplot(ssb_df_res, aes(x = Year, y = RE, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr)) +   geom_line(lwd = 1.3, lty = 2) +   geom_ribbon(alpha = 0.5) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0, lty = 2, color = "red") +   labs(x = "Year", y = "SSB Relative Error") +   theme_bw(base_size = 14) +   coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1, 1))

title: One-Step-Ahead (OSA) Residuals
text: get_osa()’s internal mode exposes two arguments: osa_method: overrides RTMB::oneStepPredict()’s method argument. Must one "oneStepGeneric", "oneStepGaussianOffMode", "oneStepGaussian" — "cdf" method deliberately disallowed numerically fragile discrete (multinomial/count) likelihoods used can silently return mis-calibrated residuals. Defaults "oneStepGeneric" discrete composition/tag families "oneStepGaussianOffMode" continuous (logistic-normal composition index-type) families. parallel: passed straight RTMB::oneStepPredict(parallel = ). Useful large composition/tag datasets OSA computation dominates runtime; verified give numerically identical residuals parallel = FALSE.
code: get_osa(model = model, data = input_list$data, index_source = "SrvIdx",        osa_method = "oneStepGaussian", parallel = TRUE)

title: Do Population Projections — Do_Population_Projection
text: n_proj_yrs Integer. Number projection years. n_pop Integer. Number populations (may exceed regions natal homing modeled). n_regions Integer. Number spatial regions. n_ages Integer. Number age classes including plus group. n_sexes Integer. Number sexes. sexratio Array `[n_pop, n_regions, n_proj_yrs, n_sexes]`. Recruitment sex ratio used allocate projected recruits sex. n_fish_fleets Integer. Number fishing fleets. do_recruits_move Integer (0 1). Whether age-1 recruits subject movement. Default = 0. recruitment Array `[n_pop, n_regions, n_yrs]`. Historical recruitment used condition stochastic projection options. terminal_NAA Array `[n_pop, n_regions, n_seas, n_ages, n_sexes]`. Fished numbers--age terminal assessment year. terminal_NAA0 Array `[n_pop, n_regions, n_seas, n_ages, n_sexes]`. Unfished numbers--age terminal assessment year. terminal_F Array `[n_regions, n_seas, n_fish_fleets]`. Terminal fishing mortality; sets F projection year 1 defines seasonal F ratios applied subsequent years. dmr Array [n_regions, n_seas, n_fish_fleets]. Discard mortality rate. Default behavior discard mortality (dmr = 0). combined ret_sel = 1, implies discarding within given fleet (catch retained). natmort Array `[n_pop, n_regions, n_proj_yrs, n_ages, n_sexes]`. Annual natural mortality--age, scaled internally season duration. natal_region Integer vector `[n_pop]`. Natal region population. WAA Array `[n_pop, n_regions, n_proj_yrs, n_seas, n_ages, n_sexes]`. Weight--age used spawning biomass calculations. WAA_fish Array `[n_pop, n_regions, n_proj_yrs, n_seas, n_ages, n_sexes, n_fish_fleets]`. Fishery weight--age used catch biomass calculations. MatAA Array `[n_pop, n_regions, n_proj_yrs, n_seas, n_ages, n_sexes]`. Maturity--age. fish_sel Array `[n_pop, n_regions, n_proj_yrs, n_seas, n_ages, n_sexes, n_fish_fleets]`. Fishery selectivity--age. ret_sel Array [n_pop, n_regions, n_proj_yrs, n_seas, n_ages, n_sexes, n_fish_fleets]. Retention selectivity--age. Default behavior corresponds full retention (ret_sel = 1), meaning captured fish retained unless otherwise specified. Movement Array `[n_pop, n_regions, n_regions, n_proj_yrs, n_seas, n_ages, n_sexes]`. Seasonal movement transition matrices. sgl_seas_spawning_movement Array `[n_pop, n_regions, n_regions, n_proj_yrs, n_ages, n_sexes]`. Spawning movement matrix applied `n_seas = 1` `n_pop > 1` redistribute fish natal grounds prior SSB calculation. stray_rate Array `[n_pop, n_proj_yrs]`. Per-population stray rate used accumulating effective SSB contributions across populations. f_ref_pt Array `[n_regions, n_proj_yrs]`. Fishing mortality reference point (e.g., F_MSY) fixed input F, depending `fmort_opt`. b_ref_pt Array `[n_pop, n_regions, n_proj_yrs]`. Biomass reference point used harvest control rules. HCR_function Function. Harvest control rule arguments `x` (SSB), `frp` (F reference point), `brp` (B reference point). recruitment_opt Character. Recruitment scenario: `"inv_gauss"`, `"mean_rec"`, `"zero"`, `"bh_rec"`. fmort_opt Character. Fishing mortality scenario: `"HCR"`, `"HCR_global"`, `"Input"`. t_spawn Numeric scalar. Fraction spawning season elapsed spawning; used mid-season SSB calculations. bh_rec_opt Named list inputs deterministic Beverton–Holt   recruitment `recruitment_opt = "bh_rec"`. list passed   directly Get_Det_Recruitment must contain   required arguments function. Required elements expected dimensions include: R0 Numeric vector [n_pop]. Unfished recruitment. h Numeric array [n_pop, n_regions]. Steepness. rec_region_prop Numeric array       [n_pop, n_regions]. Recruitment allocation across regions       (sums 1 across regions). rec_seas_prop Numeric array       [n_pop, n_seas]. Seasonal recruitment proportions       (sums 1 across seasons). SSB Numeric array       [n_pop, n_regions, n_yrs]. Historical spawning biomass,       projected SSB appended internally. WAA Array       [n_pop, n_regions, n_seas, n_ages]. Weight--age. text: Builds sparse \((n_{\text{ages}} \times n_{\text{yrs}}) \times (n_{\text{ages}} \times n_{\text{yrs}})\) precision matrix \(Q\) Gaussian Markov random field (GMRF) simultaneous autoregressive (SAR) structure across three biological dimensions: age, year, cohort (age-year diagonal). matrix constructed via path-matrix factorisation \(Q = (- B)^\top \Omega^{-1} (- B)\), \(B\) encodes partial correlations \(\Omega\) diagonal variance matrix. title: Calculate Selectivity — Get_Selex
text: Computes selectivity--bin using suite parametric, semi-parametric, non-parametric formulations. Supports constant, time-varying, fully flexible selectivity structures.

title: Calculate Selectivity — Get_Selex
code: Get_Selex(   Selex_Model,   TimeVary_Model,   pars,   ln_seldevs,   Region,   Year,   Bin,   Sex,   Wbin_bicubic = NULL,   Wyr_bicubic = NULL,   n_bin_nodes_bicubic = NULL,   n_yr_nodes_bicubic = NULL )

title: Calculate Selectivity — Get_Selex
text: Selex_Model Integer specifying selectivity model: 0 Logistic (b50, slope): \(1 / (1 + \exp(-k(\text{bin} - b_{50})))\) 1 Gamma-shaped dome (bin--peak \(b_{\max}\), curvature \(\delta\)). 2 Power function (monotonic decreasing): \(1 / \text{bin}^{\text{power}}\). 3 Logistic (b50, b95 parameterization). 4 Double-normal dome plateau flexible tails (6 parameters). 5 Non-parametric selectivity: bin-level logit parameters mapped via plogis,            optionally modified time-varying deviations. 6 Logistic selectivity asymptote:            \(\alpha / (1 + \exp(-k(\text{bin} - b_{50})))\).            Allows maximum selectivity \(\alpha \(0,1)\). 7 Logistic selectivity asymptote (b50, b95 parameterization):            \(\alpha / (1 + 19^{(b_{50} - \text{bin})/b_{95}})\).            Equivalent Model 3 scaled asymptote \(\alpha\). 8 Bicubic spline bin-node x year-node grid (see            Wbin_bicubic, Wyr_bicubic). One generalized form            covers three cases depending caller constructs            node grid interpolation weights: single smooth bin x            year surface (bicubic), time-invariant bin-spline            (n_yr_nodes == 1), bin-spline re-fit            independently within several year blocks            (n_yr_nodes == 1 within SPoRC's existing            selectivity blocks). TimeVary_Model deviation            layering applies model. TimeVary_Model Integer specifying temporal structure: 0 time variation. 1 IID deviations applied multiplicatively model parameters. 2 Random walk deviations applied multiplicatively model parameters. 3 3D GMRF (marginal variance): deviations applied multiplicatively bin level. 4 3D GMRF (conditional variance): deviations applied multiplicatively bin level. 5 Separable 2D AR(1): deviations applied multiplicatively bin level. pars Numeric vector log-scale selectivity parameters. Parameters exponentiated transformed depending model specification: Model 0 c(ln_b50, ln_slope) Model 1 c(ln_bmax, ln_delta) Model 2 c(ln_power) Model 3 c(ln_b50, ln_b95) Model 4 c(p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, p6) Model 5 c(logit_sel_1, ..., logit_sel_nbins) Model 6 c(logit_alpha, ln_b50, ln_k) Model 7 c(logit_alpha, ln_b50, ln_b95) Model 8 Flattened bin-node x year-node log-selectivity grid,       length ncol(Wyr_bicubic) * ncol(Wbin_bicubic), filled       column-major ncol(Wyr_bicubic) (rows, year nodes)       ncol(Wbin_bicubic) (columns, bin nodes) matrix. ln_seldevs Array log-scale selectivity deviations dimension   [n_regions, n_years, n_parameters_or_bins, n_sexes, 1]. TimeVary_Model = 1–2: deviations apply selectivity parameters   natural scale exponentiation. TimeVary_Model = 3–5: deviations apply multiplicatively   bin level constructed selectivity curve. Selex_Model = 5: deviations act directly bin-level logit   selectivity parameters prior logistic transformation. Region Integer region index. Year Integer year index (absolute, .e. row index Wyr_bicubic). used directly Selex_Model == 8; otherwise used index ln_seldevs. Bin Numeric vector bins (ages lengths). Sex Integer sex index. Wbin_bicubic Numeric length(Bin) x n_bin_nodes natural cubic spline weight matrix (see Get_Natural_Cubic_Spline_Weights), mapping bin-node log-selectivity values onto Bin. used Selex_Model == 8; ignored (may NULL) otherwise. Zero padding unused columns (e.g. shared parameter array padded common width across fleets/blocks) contributes nothing, since multiplied zero. Wyr_bicubic Numeric n_yrs_total x n_yr_nodes interpolation weight matrix mapping year-node log-selectivity values onto every absolute model year (rows beyond fitted block typically constructed hold boundary node constant). Row Year used call. used Selex_Model == 8; ignored (may NULL) otherwise. single-column matrix -1s (n_yr_nodes == 1) yields time-invariant bin-spline, since every year maps onto single node. n_bin_nodes_bicubic, n_yr_nodes_bicubic Integer. fleet/block's true number bin nodes / year nodes. used Selex_Model == 8. Must supplied whenever Wbin_bicubic/Wyr_bicubic may zero-padded wider specific block's grid (e.g. fleet/block shares padded storage array uses larger bicubic grid) – ncol(Wbin_bicubic)/ncol(Wyr_bicubic) give padded (shared) width, block's true node counts, using padded width reshape pars misassign flattened parameter values land (bin-node, year-node) cell. Default NULL falls back ncol(Wbin_bicubic)/ncol(Wyr_bicubic) backward compatibility padding-width mismatch possible (e.g. single bicubic block/fleet, direct unit testing).

title: Calculate Selectivity — Get_Selex
text: Numeric vector selectivity values corresponding Bin. Values natural scale normalized unless specified downstream components.

title: Calculate Selectivity — Get_Selex
text: TimeVary_Model = 0, base parametric form evaluated. TimeVary_Model = 1–2, deviations modify model parameters multiplicatively natural scale transformation. TimeVary_Model = 3–5, deviations act directly constructed selectivity curve multiplicative log-normal perturbations: $$\text{selex} = \text{selex} \cdot \exp(\delta_{r,y,b,s})$$. Selex_Model = 5, selectivity fully non-parametric: bin-specific logit parameters optionally adjusted time-varying deviations transformed via: $$\text{selex}_b = \text{logit}^{-1}(\eta_b)$$. Models 6 7 extend logistic selectivity introducing asymptote parameter \(\alpha \(0,1)\) allows selectivity saturate full vulnerability.

title: Compute a model-agnostic selectivity smoothness / dome-shape penalty (Positive Scale) — Get_Selex_Smoothness_Penalty
text: sel_vals Array selectivity values dimensioned [1, year, bin, sex, 1]. Evaluated log scale internally. wt_bin_curve Non-negative weight age/bin curvature penalty: sum squared second differences log-selectivity across bins, within year, normalized number bins. Penalizes jagged (non-smooth) selectivity--age curves. 0 (default) disables term. Requires least 3 bins effect. wt_bin_diff Non-negative weight unconditional bin first-difference penalty: sum squared first differences log-selectivity across bins, within year, normalized number bins. Unlike wt_dome (penalizes decreases), increases decreases contribute. Requires least 2 bins effect. wt_yr_diff Non-negative weight inter-annual first-difference penalty: sum squared first differences log-selectivity across years, within bin, normalized number years. Penalizes abrupt year--year jumps selectivity--bin. 0 (default) disables term. Requires least 2 years effect. wt_yr_curve Non-negative weight inter-annual second-difference (smoothness) penalty: sum squared second differences log-selectivity across years, within bin, normalized number years. Penalizes jagged (non-smooth) year--year selectivity trajectories. 0 (default) disables term. Requires least 3 years effect. wt_dome Non-negative weight dome-shape (non-monotonicity) penalty: year, penalizes decrease log-selectivity moving one bin next (.e. discourages, forbid, dome shaped dynamics. 0 (default) disables term. wt_mean_center Non-negative weight per-year mean-centering (sum--zero) regularization: year, penalizes squared mean log-selectivity across bins. 0 (default) disables term; set 10000. normalize Logical. TRUE (default), wt_bin_curve divided number bins wt_yr_diff/wt_yr_curve divided number years. SPoRC_rtmb.R always calls normalize = TRUE.

title: Set up fishing mortality, discard mortality, and catch observation inputs — Setup_Mod_Catch_and_F
text: input_list Named list $data, $par, $map, $verbose sublists, returned upstream setup functions. ObsCatch Observed aggregated catch array [n_regions x n_years x n_seas x n_fish_fleets]. Values units specified catch_units. cell UseCatch == 0 (population-specific catch used), NA entry treated genuinely missing observation – fishing assumed continued Fmort/ ln_F_devs estimated normally year – whereas true recorded value (typically 0) treated real closure: Fmort forced zero deviation estimated. See Get_Fdev_PE_loglik. UseCatch Binary indicator array [n_regions x n_years x n_seas x n_fish_fleets] controlling aggregated catch observations enter likelihood whether ln_F_devs estimated cell. 1 = use; 0 = exclude, unless ObsCatch NA cell (see ObsCatch ), case ln_F_devs still estimated ordinary active year despite fit observation. catch_units Character array [n_fish_fleets] specifying catch units per fleet. "biom" = biomass (default); "abd" = abundance. Converted internally 0/1 integer codes. UseCatch_pop Binary indicator array [n_pop x n_regions x n_years x n_seas x n_fish_fleets] controlling population-specific catch observations enter likelihood. 1 = use; 0 = exclude. ObsCatch_pop Observed population-specific catch array [n_pop x n_regions x n_years x n_seas x n_fish_fleets]. Values units specified catch_units. Use_F_pen Integer flag applying fishing mortality penalty penalise large deviations ln_F_devs. 1 = apply (default); 0 = apply. sigmaC_spec Character string specifying sharing structure ln_sigmaC (aggregated catch observation error SD). Default "fix" holds ln_sigmaC starting value (log(0.01) unless overridden via ...). Sharing options follow convention "est_shared_<dims>" <dims> underscore-separated list dimensions collapse: "r" (regions), "y" (years), "seas" (seasons), "f" (fleets), combination (e.g., "est_shared_r_y", "est_shared_r_y_seas_f"). Use "est_all" fully independent parameter per cell. warning issued "fix" selected without providing starting value .... sigmaC_pop_spec Character string specifying sharing structure ln_sigmaC_pop (population-specific catch observation error SD). Default "fix" holds ln_sigmaC_pop starting value (log(0.01) unless overridden via ...). Sharing options follow convention sigmaC_spec additional population dimension: e.g., "est_shared_pop" shares across populations, "est_shared_pop_r" shares across populations regions, "est_shared_pop_r_y_seas_f" collapses dimensions single parameter. warning issued "fix" selected without providing starting value .... sigmaF_spec Character string specifying sharing structure ln_sigmaF (fishing mortality process error SD). Default "fix" holds ln_sigmaF starting value (log(1), .e., \(\sigma_F = 1\), unless overridden via ...). warning issued "fix" selected without providing starting value .... Fdev_model Character string specifying process error structure ln_F_devs. One "iid" (default; independent deviations), "rw" (random walk; first catch-active year per region/season/fleet initialized diffuse \(N(0,5)\) prior), "ar1" (first-order autoregressive; first catch-active year drawn stationary marginal distribution, Fdev_rho_spec controls AR1 correlation parameter). Catch-active years need contiguous "rw" "ar1": transition two active years spanning gap \(d\) closed years taken elapsed gap directly (marginal transition estimating deviations closed years integrating , without actually estimating ) – see Get_Fdev_PE_loglik. warning issued "rw" "ar1" selected Use_F_pen = 0 (penalty never evaluated, process structure effect), sigmaF_spec = "fix" (process error SD estimated), ("ar1") Fdev_rho_spec = "fix" (correlation estimated) – may intentional, common oversights switching away "iid". Fdev_rho_spec Character string specifying sharing structure AR1 correlation parameter Fdev_rho, following convention sigmaF_spec. used Fdev_model = "ar1"; ignored (mapped entirely NA) otherwise. ObsDiscard Observed aggregated discard array [n_regions x n_years x n_seas x n_fish_fleets]. Values units specified discard_units. Default: NULL (discard observations). UseDiscard Binary indicator array [n_regions x n_years x n_seas x n_fish_fleets] controlling aggregated discard observations enter likelihood. 1 = use; 0 = exclude. Default: zeros. discard_units Character array [n_fish_fleets] specifying discard units per fleet. "abd" = abundance (0), "biom" = biomass (1), "abd_frac" = abundance fraction (2), "biom_frac" = biomass fraction (3, default). Converted internally integer codes. UseDiscard_pop Binary indicator array [n_pop x n_regions x n_years x n_seas x n_fish_fleets] controlling population-specific discard observations enter likelihood. 1 = use; 0 = exclude. Default: zeros. ObsDiscard_pop Observed population-specific discard array [n_pop x n_regions x n_years x n_seas x n_fish_fleets]. Values units specified discard_units. Default: NULL (population-specific discard observations). Use_dmr_pen Integer flag applying discard mortality rate penalty penalise large deviations logit_dmr_devs. 1 = apply; 0 = apply (default). Must 1 dmr_dev_spec = "est_all" 0 dmr_dev_spec = "fix". sigmaD_spec Character string specifying sharing structure ln_sigmaD (aggregated discard observation error SD). Default "fix" holds ln_sigmaD starting value (log(0.01) unless overridden via ...). Sharing options follow convention sigmaC_spec. warning issued "fix" selected without providing starting value .... sigmaD_pop_spec Character string specifying sharing structure ln_sigmaD_pop (population-specific discard observation error SD). Default "fix" holds ln_sigmaD_pop starting value (log(0.01) unless overridden via ...). Sharing options follow convention sigmaC_pop_spec. warning issued "fix" selected without providing starting value .... sigma_dmr_spec Character string specifying sharing structure ln_sigma_dmr (discard mortality rate process error SD). Default "fix" holds ln_sigma_dmr starting value (log(1) unless overridden via ...). Sharing options follow convention sigmaF_spec. warning issued "fix" selected without providing starting value .... dmr_mean_spec Character string specifying sharing/estimation structure logit_dmr_mean (logit-scale mean discard mortality rate). Default "fix" holds starting value (0, .e., DMR = 0.5 natural scale, unless overridden via ...). See do_dmr_mean_mapping sharing options. dmr_dev_spec Character string specifying sharing/estimation structure logit_dmr_devs (logit-scale annual discard mortality rate deviations). Default "fix" holds deviations zero (unless overridden via ...). Use "est" estimate deviations; requires Use_dmr_pen = 1. See do_dmr_dev_mapping sharing options. ... Optional starting value overrides catch discard related parameters.

title: Initialise model dimension settings — Setup_Mod_Dim
text: years Numeric vector calendar years included model (e.g., 1990:2024). length vector determines n_years throughout model. ages Numeric vector modelled age classes (e.g., 2:31 model spanning ages 2–31). final element treated plus-group. lens Numeric vector length bin midpoints. Set NULL length data modelled; scalar placeholder 1 stored internally case. n_pop Positive integer. Number distinct populations (default 1). Populations can independent stock-recruit relationships natal regions share spatial domain defined n_regions. natal_region Integer vector length n_pop mapping population natal region (1-indexed). Defaults applied NULL: n_regions == 1: populations assigned region 1. n_pop == n_regions: one--one mapping (1:n_pop). n_pop == 1: assigned region 1. Must supplied explicitly n_pop > 1, n_pop != n_regions, n_regions > 1, sensible default exists populations must share natal region. n_seas Positive integer. Number seasons within year (default 1). seasdur Numeric vector length n_seas giving duration season fraction year (values sum 1). Defaults 1 single season rep(1 / n_seas, n_seas) equal-length seasons n_seas > 1. n_regions Positive integer. Number spatial regions. n_sexes Integer. Number sexes; must 1 (sex-aggregated) 2 (sex-structured). n_fish_fleets Positive integer. Number fishery fleets. n_srv_fleets Positive integer. Number survey fleets. n_proj_yrs_devs Non-negative integer. Number projection years deviation parameters (ln_RecDevs, move_devs, ln_fishsel_devs, ln_srvsel_devs) allocated. Set 0 (default) projections beyond assessment period required. do_internal_comp_osa Logical. TRUE, allows OSA residuals composition datasets. Default FALSE. do_internal_conv_tag_osa Logical. TRUE, allows OSA residuals tagging datasets. Default FALSE. verbose Logical. TRUE, prints summary dimension settings console via message() setup. Default FALSE. store_config Logical. TRUE, stores configuration model. Default FALSE

title: Set up discards, fishery index, age composition, and length composition inputs — Setup_Mod_FishIdx_and_Comps
text: input_list Named list $data, $par, $map, $verbose sublists, returned upstream setup functions. ObsFishIdx Observed fishery CPUE biomass index array [n_regions × n_years × n_seas × n_fish_fleets]. ObsFishIdx_SE Standard errors ObsFishIdx log scale, dimensions ObsFishIdx. ObsFishIdx_pop Observed population-specific fishery index array [n_pop × n_regions × n_years × n_seas × n_fish_fleets]. ObsFishIdx_pop_SE Lognormal standard errors ObsFishIdx_pop, dimensions [n_pop × n_regions × n_years × n_seas × n_fish_fleets]. UseFishIdx_pop Binary indicator array [n_pop × n_regions × n_years × n_seas × n_fish_fleets]. 1 = include population-specific index likelihood; 0 = exclude. Default: zeros. fish_idx_type Character vector length n_fish_fleets specifying index type fleet. "biom" = biomass; "abd" = abundance; "none" = index fleet. UseFishIdx Binary indicator array [n_regions × n_years × n_seas × n_fish_fleets]. 1 = include index likelihood; 0 = exclude. ObsFishAgeComps Observed fishery age composition array [n_regions × n_years × n_seas × n_ages × n_sexes × n_fish_fleets]. Values may raw counts proportions; proportions, supply ISS_FishAgeComps explicitly. UseFishAgeComps Binary indicator array [n_regions × n_years × n_seas × n_fish_fleets]. 1 = fit age compositions; 0 = exclude. ISS_FishAgeComps Input sample size array [n_regions × n_years × n_seas × n_sexes × n_fish_fleets]. NULL (default), computed automatically summing ObsFishAgeComps within year–fleet–season–region cell according FishAgeComps_Type. ObsFishLenComps Observed fishery length composition array [n_regions × n_years × n_seas × n_lens × n_sexes × n_fish_fleets]. required input_list$data$fit_lengths == 1. UseFishLenComps Binary indicator array [n_regions × n_years × n_seas × n_fish_fleets]. 1 = fit length compositions; 0 = exclude. ISS_FishLenComps Input sample size array length compositions [n_regions × n_years × n_seas × n_sexes × n_fish_fleets]. NULL (default), derived automatically ObsFishLenComps. FishAgeComps_LikeType Character vector length n_fish_fleets specifying likelihood fishery age compositions. Options: "Multinomial", "Dirichlet-Multinomial", "iid-Logistic-Normal", "1d-Logistic-Normal", "2d-Logistic-Normal", "none". FishLenComps_LikeType FishAgeComps_LikeType length compositions. FishAgeComps_Type Character vector defining age composition structure (aggregation level) fleet time period. element must follow format "<type>_Year_<start>-<end>_Fleet_<f>" "<type>_Year_<start>-terminal_Fleet_<f>". Valid types: "agg" Aggregated across regions sexes     (incompatible "2d-Logistic-Normal"). "spltRspltS" Split region sex. "spltRjntS" Split region, summed jointly across sexes. "none" composition data fleet period. Example: c("spltRjntS_Year_1-10_Fleet_1", "agg_Year_11-terminal_Fleet_1"). FishLenComps_Type format options FishAgeComps_Type applied length compositions. code: Setup_Mod_Movement(   input_list,   move_type = 0,   do_recruits_move = 0,   use_fixed_movement = 0,   Fixed_Movement = NA,   Use_Movement_Prior = 0,   Movement_prior = NULL,   Movement_popblk_spec = "constant",   Movement_ageblk_spec = "constant",   Movement_yearblk_spec = "constant",   Movement_seasblk_spec = "constant",   Movement_sexblk_spec = "constant",   cont_vary_movement = "none",   Movement_cont_pe_pars_spec = "none",   ctmc_move_dat = NULL,   adjacency_mat = NULL,   area_r = rep(1, input_list$data$n_regions),   diffusion_formula = NULL,   preference_formula = NULL,   ctmc_diffusion_bounds = 0,   ... )

title: Set up movement model inputs and parameter structures — Setup_Mod_Movement
text: input_list Named list $data, $par, $map, $verbose sublists, returned upstream setup functions. move_type Integer. Movement model formulation: 0 = unstructured Markov; 1 = CTMC. Default 0. do_recruits_move Integer flag. 0 = age-1 fish move (default); movement deviations CTMC rows minimum age fixed zero. 1 = recruits participate movement. use_fixed_movement Integer flag. 0 = estimate movement (default); 1 = fix movement rates Fixed_Movement map movement parameters NA. Fixed_Movement Numeric array externally supplied movement probability matrices, dimensioned [n_pop × n_regions × n_regions × n_years × n_seas × n_ages × n_sexes]. [n_regions × n_regions] slice must row-stochastic (rows sum 1). Required use_fixed_movement = 1. NA (default), identity matrix (movement) constructed internally. Use_Movement_Prior Integer flag. 1 = apply Dirichlet priors movement row probabilities; 0 = priors (default). Requires Movement_prior. Movement_prior Data frame Dirichlet prior concentration parameters. Required columns: pop, region_from, year, seas, age, sex, alpha, alpha list-column element numeric vector length n_regions giving Dirichlet concentration transitions region_from. Values near 1 uninformative; larger values concentrate prior toward equal movement. used Use_Movement_Prior = 1. Movement_popblk_spec "constant" (default, shared across populations) list integer vectors partitioning populations blocks. Example: list(c(1, 2), 3) shares parameters populations 1 2 estimates separate parameter population 3. Ignored move_type = 1. Movement_ageblk_spec "constant" (default) list integer vectors defining age blocks. Example: list(1:4, 5:10) creates juvenile block (ages 1–4) adult block (ages 5–10). Ignored move_type = 1. Movement_yearblk_spec "constant" (default) list integer vectors defining year blocks discrete structural breaks movement. residual annual variation, use cont_vary_movement instead. Ignored move_type = 1. Movement_seasblk_spec "constant" (default) list integer vectors defining season blocks. Example: list(c(1, 2), c(3, 4)) groups winter/spring summer/fall. Ignored move_type = 1. Movement_sexblk_spec "constant" (default, sex-invariant) list integer vectors defining sex blocks. Example: list(1, 2) estimates sex-specific movement independently. Ignored move_type = 1. cont_vary_movement Character string specifying structure continuous iid movement deviations added top fixed-effect movement surface. Default "none". Options: "none" deviations. "iid_y" Year-varying; shared across pop, age, sex, season. "iid_a" Age-varying; shared across pop, year, sex, season. "iid_y_a" Year \(\times\) age. "iid_y_a_s" Year \(\times\) age \(\times\) sex. "iid_y_seas_a_s" Year \(\times\) season \(\times\) age \(\times\) sex. "iid_p_y", "iid_p_a", "iid_p_y_a", "iid_p_y_a_s", "iid_p_y_seas_a_s" Population-specific analogues . Movement_cont_pe_pars_spec Character string specifying estimation process-error variance cont_vary_movement deviations. One : "none" process-error parameters; use cont_vary_movement = "none". "fix" Parameters initialised estimated; fixes     deviation variance starting value. "est_shared" Single variance estimated, shared across     dimensions. "est_all" variance parameters estimated independently,     dimensioned [n_pop × n_regions × n_seas × n_ages × n_sexes]. ctmc_move_dat Data frame required move_type = 1. row corresponds unique pop–region–year–season–age–sex combination. Required columns: pop, regions, years, seas, ages, sexes, plus covariate columns referenced diffusion_formula preference_formula. Projection years exceeding n_years automatically capped final estimation year prevent spline extrapolation. adjacency_mat Square numeric matrix [n_regions × n_regions] 1 indicating allowed transition 0 indicating direct connection; diagonal 0. Required move_type = 1. move_type = 0 fully connected matrix constructed automatically. area_r Numeric vector length n_regions giving area region, used scale CTMC diffusion rates. Required move_type = 1. Default: rep(1, n_regions). diffusion_formula R formula defining linear predictor CTMC diffusion (\(\theta\)) component (e.g., ~ bs(depth, df = 4)). right-hand-side variables must present ctmc_move_dat. Required move_type = 1. preference_formula R formula defining linear predictor CTMC habitat-preference (taxis, \(\gamma\)) component. variables must present ctmc_move_dat. Required move_type = 1. ctmc_diffusion_bounds Integer flag. 1 = apply bounds diffusion parameters ensure CTMC generator matrix valid Metzler matrix (non-negative -diagonal entries). 0 = bounds (default). ... Optional starting value overrides, passed name. Recognised arguments: move_pars Array [n_pop × n_regions × (n_regions-1) × n_years × n_seas × n_ages × n_sexes]. Default: 0 (equal movement logit scale). log_move_diffusion_pars Vector length n_theta. Default: log(0.1). move_preference_pars Vector length n_gamma. Default: 0. move_devs Array [n_pop × n_regions × (n_regions-1) × (n_years + n_proj_yrs_devs) × n_seas × n_ages × n_sexes]. Default: 0. move_pe_pars Array [n_pop × n_regions × n_seas × n_ages × n_sexes]. Default: 0.

what: Set up the recruitment module and associated processes — Setup_Mod_Rec
title: Set up the recruitment module and associated processes — Setup_Mod_Rec

Delegates parameter mapping family internal helpers (do_sigmaR_mapping, do_RecDevs_mapping, do_InitDevs_mapping, do_h_mapping, do_sexratio_pars_mapping, do_rec_region_prop_mapping, do_rec_seas_prop_mapping). Must called Setup_Mod_Dim Setup_Mod_Biologicals, model compilation.

title: Set up the recruitment module and associated processes — Setup_Mod_Rec
text: input_list Named list $data, $par, $map, $verbose sublists, returned upstream setup functions. Population, region, age, year, season dimensions must already defined $data. rec_model Character string (required). Stock-recruit relationship: "mean_rec" Fixed mean recruitment; stock-recruit     relationship. Steepness automatically fixed estimated. "bh_rec" Beverton-Holt stock-recruit relationship. rec_dd Density-dependence structure. Default "global". "local" Independent stock-recruit relationship per     population. Required n_pop > 1. "global" Single pooled spawner-recruit relationship     across regions. Constrains h_spec,     RecDevs_spec, InitDevs_spec shared fixed     options n_regions > 1. rec_lag Integer. Lag spawning biomass recruitment (seasons). 1 (default) classic lagged case: recruitment uses SSB rec_lag seasons prior may enter season. 0 age-0 recruitment: recruitment uses year's SSB, SSB known spawn_seas reached, recruits may enter spawn_seas later season – use_fixed_rec_seas_prop = 1, fixed_rec_seas_prop must zero spawn_seas; estimated, enforced structurally via restricted softmax (see do_rec_seas_prop_mapping). Use_h_prior Integer (0/1). Whether normal priors steepness applied. relevant rec_model = "bh_rec". Default 0. h_prior Data frame steepness prior parameters. Required columns: pop, region, mu, sd. Ignored Use_h_prior = 0. Default NULL. rec_region_prop_spec Character NULL. Regional recruitment dispersal structure. Default NULL (estimate proportions freely). See do_rec_region_prop_mapping full option descriptions including "no_dispersal". Stored $data$rec_region_prop_spec: 0 = full dispersal, 1 = dispersal. use_rec_region_prop_prior Integer (0/1). Whether Dirichlet priors applied regional recruitment proportions. valid n_regions = 1. Default 0. rec_region_prop_prior Data frame Dirichlet prior concentration parameters. Required columns: pop alpha, alpha list-column length-n_regions vectors. Ignored use_rec_region_prop_prior = 0. Default NULL. rec_seas_prop_spec Character NULL. Seasonal recruitment apportionment structure. Default "fix". See do_rec_seas_prop_mapping full option descriptions including "est_shared_pop". use_rec_seas_prop_prior Integer (0/1). Whether Dirichlet priors applied seasonal recruitment proportions. valid n_seas = 1. rec_lag = 0 spawn_seas > 1, prior evaluated seasons spawn_seas:n_seas (seasons spawn_seas structurally zero, estimated). Default 0. rec_seas_prop_prior Data frame Dirichlet prior concentration parameters seasonal proportions. Required columns: pop alpha. Ignored use_rec_seas_prop_prior = 0. Default NULL. use_fixed_rec_seas_prop Integer (0/1). Whether fixed (non-estimated) seasonal proportions fixed_rec_seas_prop used. Automatically reset 0 warning rec_seas_prop_spec requests estimation. Default 1. fixed_rec_seas_prop Array [n_pop x n_seas]. Fixed seasonal recruitment proportions used use_fixed_rec_seas_prop = 1. Default: recruitment assigned season 1. rec_lag = 0 spawn_seas > 1, must zero every season spawn_seas – error raised otherwise. do_rec_bias_ramp Integer (0/1). Whether recruitment bias ramp applied ln_RecDevs account reduced information early terminal years. Default 0. bias_year Numeric. Calendar year bias ramp reaches maximum correction. used do_rec_bias_ramp = 1. Default NA. max_bias_ramp_fct Numeric \([0, 1]\). Maximum bias correction factor applied bias_year. Default 1. sigmaR_switch Integer. Year index \(\sigma_R\) switches early-period value (index 1) late-period value (index 2). \(\leq 1\), single \(\sigma_R\) applied throughout. Default 1. dont_est_recdev_last Non-negative integer. Number terminal years recruitment deviations estimated. Automatically overridden 0 n_proj_yrs_devs > 0, since projected deviation years penalised toward mean effectively estimated regardless. Default 0. init_age_strc Equilibrium initialisation method. Default 2. 0/"iterative" Iterates population     approximate equilibrium. Slowest general. 1/"scalar_no_move" Scalar geometric series     assuming movement. 2/"matrix" Matrix geometric series incorporating     movement. Recommended default spatial models. 3/"scalar_plus_only" Scalar geometric series     movement plus group. equil_init_age_strc Plus-group treatment stochastic initialisation. Default 1. 0/"equil" Deterministic equilibrium;     ln_InitDevs estimated. 1/"stoch_no_plus" Stochastic deviations     ages except plus group. 2/"stoch_all" Stochastic deviations ages     including plus group. 3/"stoch_shared_ages" Stochastic deviations     user-defined age sharing via init_age_devs_shared. Deviations     estimated independently across populations regions,     ages sharing value init_age_devs_shared     constrained single parameter. plus group automatically     fixed; include NA init_age_devs_shared     plus-group position fix , share preceding age     repeating index (e.g. c(1:42, rep(42, 9))). Requires     init_age_devs_shared non-NULL. init_F_prop Numeric array [n_regions x n_seas x n_fish_fleets]. Seasonal distribution fishing mortality applied equilibrium initialisation fleet. Default: zero seasons fleets. sigmaR_spec Character. Estimation structure \(\sigma_R\), stored ln_sigmaR [2 x n_pop x n_regions], index 1 = initial deviation period index 2 = annual deviation period. Default "est_all". See do_sigmaR_mapping full option descriptions. InitDevs_spec Character NULL. Sharing structure initial age-structure deviations ln_InitDevs [n_pop x n_regions x (n_ages - 1)]. Default NULL (estimate independently). See do_InitDevs_mapping full option descriptions. RecDevs_spec Character NULL. Sharing structure annual recruitment deviations ln_RecDevs [n_pop x n_regions x n_years]. Default NULL (estimate independently). See do_RecDevs_mapping full option descriptions. h_spec Character NULL. Sharing structure Beverton-Holt steepness steepness_h [n_pop x n_regions], parameterised bounded logit space \((0.2, 1)\). Default NULL (estimate population n_pop > 1, region n_pop = 1). Ignored rec_model = "mean_rec". See do_h_mapping full option descriptions. sgl_seas_spawning_movement Spawning movement array [n_pop x n_regions x n_regions x n_years x n_ages x n_sexes]. [p, , r, y, , s] slice row-stochastic movement matrix giving probability fish origin region spawning region r. NA (default), 100% natal homing assumed array constructed internally. t_spawn Numeric. Spawn timing fraction season elapsed spawning. 0 (default) = spawning mortality; 1 = spawning mortality. stray_rate_spec Character string. Estimation structure stray_rate_pars [n_pop x max_stray_blocks], parameterised logit scale. Ignored use_fixed_stray_rate = 1 n_pop = 1. Default "fix". Options: "fix" parameters fixed starting values (mapped     NA). Use alongside use_fixed_stray_rate = 0     hold stray rates specified value without estimating. "est_all" Estimate independently per population x block.     Produces one parameter per population per unique block. "est_shared_pop" Single parameter per block, shared across     populations. Requires identical block structures across     populations – error raised block indices differ. stray_rate_blocks Character vector length n_pop defining temporal block structure stray rate parameters. Valid formats: "none_Pop_x" Constant stray rate population x     across years (single block). "Block_k_Year_a-b_Pop_x" Block k applies years     b population x. Use     "terminal" place end year extend     final model year. Default: single constant block every population. Note: stray rate generally unidentifiable fisheries data alone. Time-blocking provided completeness regularisation via use_stray_rate_prior penalty setup strongly recommended whenever stray_rate_spec != "fix". use_fixed_stray_rate Integer (0/1). Whether stray rates supplied fixed external array (fixed_stray_rate) rather estimated model parameters. Default 1 (fixed), preserving existing behaviour. Set 0 estimate stray rates via stray_rate_pars. fixed_stray_rate Array [n_pop x n_years]. Fixed stray rate values used use_fixed_stray_rate = 1. Values \([0, 1]\). Default: 0 (straying) populations years. Ignored use_fixed_stray_rate = 0. use_stray_rate_prior Integer (0/1). Whether Beta priors applied estimated stray rate parameters. relevant use_fixed_stray_rate = 0 n_pop > 1. error raised use_stray_rate_prior = 1 alongside use_fixed_stray_rate = 1 since stray_rate_pars estimated. Default 0. stray_rate_prior Data frame Beta prior parameters stray rates. Required columns: pop (population index), block (block index matching stray_rate_blocks), mu (prior mean, \((0,1)\)), sd (prior standard deviation). One row per population x block combination penalise. Ignored use_stray_rate_prior = 0. Default NULL. spawn_seas Integer. Season index spawning occurs. Default 1. sexratio_spec Character. Estimation structure sex ratio parameters sexratio_pars [n_pop x n_regions x n_blocks]. Default "fix". See do_sexratio_pars_mapping full option descriptions. Must "fix" n_sexes = 1. sexratio_blocks Character vector defining temporal block structure sex ratio parameters. One entry per population-region combination. Valid formats: "none_Pop_x_Region_x" Constant sex ratio population     x region x (single block across years). "Block_k_Year_a-b_Pop_x_Region_x" Block k     applies years b. Use "terminal"     place end year extend final model year. Default: single constant block every population-region combination. use_rinit Integer (0/1). Whether separate initial recruitment scalar ln_rinit used initialise population independently recruitment ln_global_R0. 0 (default), ln_rinit fixed ln_global_R0 governs initialisation recruitment. 1, ln_rinit ln_global_R0 estimated, ln_rinit used exclusively equilibrium initialisation ln_global_R0 used stock-recruit relationship. init_age_devs_shared Integer vector length n_ages - 1 specifying explicit parameter-sharing structure ln_InitDevs along age dimension. element gives factor level assigned age position; positions sharing integer value constrained single estimated parameter. Used conjunction equil_init_age_strc = 3 ("stoch_shared_ages"), activates user-defined age sharing still estimating deviations independently across populations regions. sharing structure also respected InitDevs_spec options: "est_shared_r" applies vector per population (population-level offset pops remain independent), "est_shared_pop_r" applies globally (offset, pops regions share parameters). typical use case replicating ADMB models ages beyond data plus group share last estimated deviation, e.g. c(1:42, rep(42, 9)) 52-age model 43 data ages, giving 42 free parameters. NULL (default), age sharing follows standard behaviour determined equil_init_age_strc alone. use_r0_prior Integer (0/1). Whether apply lognormal prior R0 populations. Default 0. r0_prior Data frame columns pop (population index), mu (prior mean natural scale), sd (prior SD log scale). Required use_r0_prior = 1. ... Optional named starting values parameters. : ln_global_R0 [n_pop], ln_rinit [n_pop], rec_region_prop_pars [n_pop x (n_regions - 1)], rec_seas_prop_pars [n_pop x (n_seas - 1)], steepness_h [n_pop x n_regions] (bounded logit scale), ln_InitDevs [n_pop x n_regions x (n_ages - 1)], ln_RecDevs [n_pop x n_regions x n_years], ln_sigmaR [2 x n_pop x n_regions], sexratio_pars [n_pop x n_regions x n_blocks]. Unspecified parameters use internal defaults.
